newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T sees U.S. tobacco deal as isolated.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T sees U.S. tobacco deal as isolated.

text.p: Britain's B.A.T Industries said on Wednesday a landmark settlement of legal claims against the tobacco industry in the United States announced in June was unlikely to affect other countries.

"Shareholders may well be concerned about whether the proposed resolution will also affect other countries. We do not consider that it will," said chairman Lord Cairns in a statement attached to the group's half-year results.

There is uncertainty in the short term about the American proposals so B.A.T decided on an unchanged dividend of 10 pence per share at the half year stage, said Cairns. The company plans to pay a final dividend of no less than 16.0 pence.
American tobacco companies agreed with state attorney's to settle most legal claims against them in return for payments totalling 230 billion pounds ($374.9 billion) over 25 years.

The group announced pre-tax profits of 1.247 billion pounds in the six months to June 30 down 64 million or five percent on the first half of 1996, due mainly to the 61 million impact of the strength of sterling on foreign exchange markets.

Trading profit from tobacco rose six percent to 800 million pounds if the 22 million costs of closing a cigarette factory in Berlin and 21 million for a legal settlement in Mississippi are excluded. Total cigarette volumes were flat at 340 billion.

In financial services, total trading profit rose 6 percent to 593 million with good performances from Farmers in the United States, Allied Dunbar in Britain and Canada Trust. Profit from the general business was ahead four percent at 346 million and from the life companies nine percent at 247 million. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
